movement.unit: basis points (from/to in %, delta in bps)

basis: Group net interest margin, cash basis, continuing operations. Comparator: FY25 (year ended 30 June 2025) as restated in the FY26 Profit Announcement; the restated value (2.08%) equals the value the FY25 Profit Announcement first reported. NIM = net interest income divided by average interest earning assets, with mortgage offset balances netted down (FY26 PA, PDF p.28 footnotes; definition at FY26 PA, PDF p.100, note 4).

drivers.name: Liquid asset growth (mix, broadly earnings-neutral)
drivers.narrative: Average liquid assets rose $15bn (9%) to $187bn. Liquids yield less than loans, so they dilute the ratio but add little net interest income. Both documents quantify this at -3 bps.

citations.quote: Excluding growth in liquid assets, which have broadly neutral impacts on net interest income, net interest margin was stable.
Liquid asset average balances increased $15 billion or 9% on the prior year to $187 billion.
Increase in liquid assets (3)

drivers.name: Institutional reverse-repo growth (mix, broadly earnings-neutral)
drivers.narrative: Average institutional reverse sale and repurchase agreement balances rose $11bn. The presentation quantifies this at -1 bp inside 'Liquids & repos (4)'. The profit announcement puts this effect inside its -2 bps Treasury and Markets item and does not give a separate number.

citations.quote: Increase in institutional repos (1)
+$15bn increase in average liquid assets and +$11bn increase in average institutional repos in FY26 vs FY25.
Treasury and Markets: Decreased margin by 2 basis points due to lower risk management income in Treasury and growth in reverse sale and repurchase agreement balances.

drivers.name: Asset pricing (lending margin compression)
drivers.narrative: Home lending pricing cut 4 bps and business and institutional lending pricing cut 1 bp. The profit announcement attributes the compression primarily to competition. The presentation splits the home lending 4 bps into competition (-3 bps) and cash rate lag (-1 bp).

citations.quote: Asset pricing: Decreased margin by 5 basis points driven by home lending pricing (down 4 basis points) and business and institutional lending pricing (down 1 basis point), primarily reflecting the impact of competition.
Home loan competition (3) Impact of cash rate lag (1) Business & Insto. lending (1)

drivers.name: Funding costs
drivers.narrative: Funding costs made no net contribution across the full year. (In 2H26 alone they added 2 bps from rising rates, offset by deposit mix, but the full-year effect is flat.)

citations.quote: Funding costs: Flat.
Funding costs

drivers.name: Portfolio mix
drivers.narrative: Strong growth in higher-margin business lending improved asset mix, and strong deposit growth improved funding mix. Business and corporate average loans grew $27bn (10%).

citations.quote: Portfolio mix: Increased margin by 2 basis points driven by favourable asset mix from strong growth in business lending and favourable funding mix from strong growth in deposits.
Favourable asset mix and deposits growing faster than lending

drivers.name: Basis risk
drivers.narrative: No net contribution. The June 2026 average BBSW/OIS spread was 6 bps, below the long-term average of 20 bps.

citations.quote: Basis risk: Flat.
Jun 26 average BBSW/OIS spread = 6bpts

drivers.name: Capital, replicating portfolio and other (interest rate risk hedging)
drivers.narrative: Replicating portfolio earnings added 4 bps and capital (equity) hedge earnings added 1 bp. The benefit came from higher portfolio rates and volume; 3-year and 5-year swap rates rose in FY26 and the Australian cash rate rose 50 bps on a spot basis.

citations.quote: Capital, Replicating and Other: Increased margin by 5 basis points driven by higher earnings on the replicating portfolio due to changes in portfolio rate and volume (up 4 basis points) and higher earnings on capital hedges (up 1 basis point).
Replicating portfolio 4 Higher earnings on capital 1
Returns from the replicating portfolio and equity hedge are sensitive to 3 year and 5 year swap rates which increased in FY26
During the financial year ended 30 June 2026 the official cash rate in Australia has increased 50 basis points on a spot basis

drivers.name: Treasury and Markets (excluding repo balance growth)
drivers.narrative: Lower risk management income in Treasury. The presentation shows -1 bp for Treasury & Markets after it moves the repo balance effect into 'Liquids & repos'. The profit announcement shows -2 bps because its Treasury and Markets item includes the repo balance growth.

citations.quote: Treasury & Markets ... (1)
Treasury and Markets: Decreased margin by 2 basis points due to lower risk management income in Treasury and growth in reverse sale and repurchase agreement balances.

disagreements.topic: Classification of the institutional repo drag
disagreements.profit_announcement: Liquids -3 bps; Treasury and Markets -2 bps (repo growth included in Treasury and Markets).
disagreements.results_presentation: Liquids & repos -4 bps (liquids -3, repos -1); Treasury & Markets -1 bp.
disagreements.reason: The presentation isolates the earnings-neutral repo volume effect from real Treasury and Markets income performance. This matches the bank's own underlying-margin narrative on PA PDF p.9 ('excluding growth in liquid assets and institutional reverse sale and repurchase agreements'). The two schemes agree on the combined -5 bps and on the -3 bps total.

disagreements.topic: Attribution inside the -4 bps home lending pricing item
disagreements.profit_announcement: Home lending pricing -4 bps, 'primarily reflecting the impact of competition' (PDF p.28).
disagreements.results_presentation: Home loan competition -3 bps plus cash rate lag -1 bp (PDF p.60).
disagreements.reason: The presentation gives finer granularity and does not conflict with the PA total of -4 bps; the PA uses 'primarily', which allows a non-competition component.

disagreements.profit_announcement: 'Excluding growth in liquid assets ... net interest margin was stable' (PDF p.28); p.9 excludes liquids and repos and says 'broadly stable'.
disagreements.results_presentation: Underlying NIM up 1 bp: rebased FY25 2.04% to FY26 2.05% (slide 6, PDF p.6; note 4, PDF p.130).
disagreements.reason: The presentation's +1 bp uses a rebased FY25 that removes the 4 bps liquids/repo mix impact. 'Stable' and '+1 bp' describe the same underlying result at different rounding.

limitations: Waterfall values come from chart data labels in the extracted PDF text. Label order in extraction was scrambled; each value was cross-checked against the narrative text and against the arithmetic sum (-3 bps).
All contributions are rounded to whole basis points by the bank; unrounded components may not sum exactly.

The FY26 PA states comparatives are restated to conform to current-period presentation (PDF p.11). The restated FY25 NIM (2.08%) matches the originally published FY25 value (FY25 PA, PDF p.28), so restatement risk to the comparator is low.

The appendix decomposition (interest spread +6 bps to 1.52%, benefit of interest-free liabilities -9 bps to 0.53%; FY26 PA PDF p.100) is a different lens on the same -3 bps and was not reconciled to the driver waterfall.
Divisional NIM movements (e.g. RBS, Business Banking, IB&M, ASB) were not decomposed; this attribution is Group-level only.
Sub-driver splits sourced only from the presentation (repos -1 bp; home loan competition -3 bps vs cash rate lag -1 bp) have no corroborating number in the profit announcement.
